title: How to Grill Delicate Goat Cheese Logs Using a Non-Stick Mat
meta_description: Learn how to grill goat cheese on mat for a perfectly melted center and golden crust. Stop the cheese from slipping through the grates with our guide.
html:
There is something magical about the combination of tangy, creamy goat cheese and the smokiness of a backyard grill. However, if you’ve ever tried to put a log of chèvre directly on grill grates, you know the struggle: it either sticks to the metal or, more likely, melts right through the bars and disappears into the coals.

The secret to success is using a barrier. When you grill goat cheese on mat, you create a stable, non-stick surface that allows the cheese to soften and brown without the risk of a meltdown. This is where BBQ Grill Mats come into play, turning a high-risk appetizer into a foolproof crowd-pleaser.

Why You Need a Non-Stick Mat for Goat Cheese

Goat cheese is temperamental. Unlike Halloumi or Paneer, which have high melting points and hold their shape, standard goat cheese logs soften quickly. The moment the heat hits, the edges liquefy. Without a mat, you're fighting a losing battle against gravity.

Using BBQ Grill Mats prevents flare-ups and eliminates the "stick-and-tear" effect. Instead of the cheese clinging to the grate and ripping apart when you try to flip it, the non-stick surface allows the log to slide easily. This means you get a consistent golden-brown crust on the outside while the inside becomes warm and gooey.

Preparing Your Goat Cheese for the Grill

To get the best results, don't just throw a cold log on the heat. Preparation is key to ensuring the cheese doesn't over-melt before it browns.

First, keep your goat cheese logs chilled until the moment they hit the grill. Cold cheese takes a few extra seconds to melt, giving the exterior more time to sear. I recommend slicing the logs into thick rounds, about 1 inch thick. If the rounds are too thin, they will soften too quickly; too thick, and the center stays cold.

For added flavor, I like to press a few fresh thyme leaves or a pinch of cracked black pepper into the top of each round. Since you're using a mat, you don't have to worry about these small herbs falling through the grates and causing smoke.

Step-by-Step: How to Grill Goat Cheese on Mat

Now that your cheese is prepped and your grill is preheated to medium-high, it's time to cook. Follow these steps for a perfect sear:

  • Position the Mat: Place your BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grill grates. Ensure the mat is flat and secure.
  • Add the Cheese: Carefully place your chilled goat cheese rounds onto the mat, leaving about an inch of space between each piece.
  • The First Sear: Grill for about 2 to 3 minutes. Avoid the temptation to move them; let the heat create a golden crust.
  • The Flip: Using a thin metal spatula, gently slide under the cheese and flip it over. This is where the non-stick surface really shines.
  • Final Touch: Grill for another 2 minutes on the second side. Remove them immediately once they are golden brown.

Serving Suggestions for Grilled Goat Cheese

Grilled goat cheese is delicious on its own, but it truly shines when paired with contrasting textures and flavors. Because the cheese is warm and rich, you want something acidic or sweet to balance the palate.

My favorite way to serve these is on a toasted baguette slice topped with a dollop of fig jam and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. The sweetness of the jam cuts through the tang of the cheese perfectly. Alternatively, place the grilled rounds atop a bed of fresh arugula with sliced pears and toasted walnuts for a sophisticated summer salad.

If you're hosting a party, serve them as "crostini sliders" with a thin slice of grilled peach on top. The heat from the cheese slightly warms the peach, creating a gourmet appetizer that looks like it came from a bistro.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your BBQ Grill Mats

One of the best parts about using BBQ Grill Mats is that they save you from scrubbing the grill grates after cooking sticky foods. Once you've finished grilling your cheese, let the mat cool down before removing it from the grill.

Most of the residue will slide right off. For a deeper clean, use warm soapy water and a soft sponge. Avoid using abrasive steel wool, as you want to preserve the non-stick coating for your next session. Once dry, store them flat so they don't warp, and they'll be ready for your next backyard feast.

FAQ

Can I use parchment paper instead of a grill mat?

No. Parchment paper is not designed for the direct, high heat of a grill and can ignite or burn through quickly. A dedicated non-stick grill mat is made from heat-resistant materials specifically for outdoor cooking.

What is the best type of goat cheese to use?

A firm, log-style chèvre is best. Avoid the soft, spreadable goat cheese found in tubs, as these lack the structure to hold their shape even on a mat.

Why is my goat cheese still sticking to the mat?

This usually happens if the mat isn't preheated. Make sure the mat is hot before adding the cheese; this creates the "sear" that releases the food from the surface more efficiently.
